conviction_note: Mild up lean (p_up 54 on a 5.2% abs move): the Q3 consensus ($2.72-2.73 EPS on $3.18B) sits just below Q2's actual run-rate ($2.76 on $3.18B at a 21.9% adj op margin), and the company beat by $0.19 and $0.16 the last two quarters and raised each time. That is offset by a full-year street number (~$10.84) already in the upper half of the $10.60-10.90 guide, so a raise is expected, and by a reaction record where beat-and-raise paid +10.0, +1.5 and -2.3. The findings sum to +0.30 and the scaled number is +0.42. They agree in sign and differ only by rounding.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $2.72 / revenue $3.18B (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/wab, whisper $2.76); $2.73 EPS (fn2.ai, https://fn2.ai/earnings/wab/2026-q2/analysts/all), which also shows Q4 at $2.64. Two sources agree within a cent. Company guide FY26 adj EPS $10.60-10.90 and sales $12.3-12.6B (https://www.wabteccorp.com/newsroom/press-releases/wabtec-reports-strong-second-quarter-2026-results). Implied street FY = 2.71 + 2.76 + 2.73 + 2.64 = ~$10.84, upper half of the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest is small. Equibles shows 3.0M shares at the 2026-04-30 settlement with 2.91 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/wab/shortinterest). That is about 1.8% of ~170M shares, so this is not a crowded short. No October settlement was found. Baseline skew is -2.03 vol points ('upside paid'), but total front-expiry open interest is only 281 contracts with a 15.6% ATM spread, so the skew says little. The run-up is -2.48% over 5 days and -3.56% over 20 days; the stock is 8.6% off its 52-week high and 44% above its 52-week low. Sell-side: 33 ratings, 20 bullish. In the run-in, Citi trimmed its target to $338 from $341 on 2026-10-08 and JPM raised to $320 from $315 (Neutral) on 2026-09-21.

findings.finding: Q3 consensus EPS of $2.72-2.73 on $3.18B revenue sits below Q2's actual $2.76 on the same $3.18B of revenue at a 21.9% adj op margin. Q3 2025's margin (21.0%) was in line with Q2 2025's (~21.1%), and Q2 2026's margin was up +0.8pt y/y. Holding the Q2 margin into Q3 therefore implies about $2.75-2.78, a beat of ~$0.03-0.06. The caveat: management said margin growth accelerates meaningfully in Q4, not Q3, so Q3 margin expansion may be smaller.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: beat by $0.19 and raised, +1.51%. Q2 2026: beat by $0.16 and raised, with backlog +41%, +10.04%. Q3 2025: beat by $0.04 and raised/tightened, -2.31%. Beats have been paid unevenly.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits below the latest quarterly run-rate, even though the company has beaten by $0.16-0.19 for two quarters. If the run-rate were priced, Q3 consensus would sit at $2.76+, and the whisper ($2.76) would not be above consensus. Partly priced: the whisper already shows it.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 margin (21.0%) and segment detail are from a separate document, the Q3 2025 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/943452/000162828025045773/a3q25pressreleaseword.htm). The whisper of $2.76 is from https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/wab. The Q2 call commentary (Q3 revenue growth slightly above Q4, margin acceleration in Q4) is from https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/wabtec-q2-earnings-call-highlights and cuts against the size.

findings.finding: Street full-year EPS already sits above the guide midpoint. Q1 $2.71 + Q2 $2.76 + Q3 consensus $2.73 + Q4 consensus $2.64 = ~$10.84, against a $10.60-10.90 guide with a $10.75 midpoint. To read as a positive, a raise has to move the midpoint to about $10.85-10.90 or higher. A raise only to the top of the existing range, or a reaffirmation, would land below what the street already models.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance was raised at Q1 2026 (+1.51%), Q2 2026 (+10.04%) and Q3 2025 (-2.31%). The guide direction has been up at every recent print, so the market is conditioned to expect a raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic on public numbers, so mostly priced. It sets the bar for the guide rather than the outcome. If the market expected only a token raise, FY street EPS would sit at or below the $10.75 midpoint, not at $10.84.
findings.independence: Guide range is from the company's Q2 release (https://www.wabteccorp.com/newsroom/press-releases/wabtec-reports-strong-second-quarter-2026-results). Q1 adj EPS of $2.71 is from the Q1 release (https://www.wabteccorp.com/newsroom/press-releases/wabtec-reports-first-quarter-2026-results).

findings.finding: Q3 brought several publicly announced orders that should lift the Q3 backlog (which was $30.93B multi-year and $9.14B 12-month at June 30). They are a more-than-$700M long-term services agreement with CTG for the Simandou line in Guinea (2026-09-22, Wabtec's largest services contract in Africa), a $254M fleet renewal by MRS Logistica in Brazil (2026-09-23), and an expanded Norfolk Southern DC-to-AC modernization of 33 units (2026-08-26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +10.04% on Q2 2026 came with multi-year backlog up 41.7% y/y, so backlog is a line this stock has paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: Each order was announced publicly and is priced on its own. What is not observable is the quarter's total orders and book-to-bill. The Q3 orders known so far are under $1.1B against ~$3.2B of quarterly revenue, so the backlog headline depends on unannounced flow orders.
findings.independence: The Norfolk Southern order is a separate document (https://www.wabteccorp.com/newsroom/press-releases/norfolk-southern-and-wabtec-expand-locomotive-modernization-program, 2026-08-26). The MRS Brazil order comes from the MarketScreener news feed (https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/WESTINGHOUSE-AIR-BRAKE-TE-14842/news/, 2026-09-23).

findings.finding: US rail traffic stayed firm through Q3. AAR year-to-date US carloads were +2.7% and intermodal +4.4% through week 40, and the week ending Oct 10 showed carloads +3.4% and intermodal +10.4%. Wabtec cited carloads up ~4% in Q2 as support for locomotive operations, services and aftermarket demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history; the Freight services/components line is not a stated driver of past reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public weekly series, so it is largely priced. It is filed as an industry proxy for the components and aftermarket mix, which neither the company nor a counterparty has confirmed for Q3.
findings.independence: Proxy. AJOT carries the same AAR release (https://www.ajot.com/news/aar-reports-rail-traffic-for-the-week-ending-october-10-2026), so the two count as one source.

findings.finding: The North American railcar build is weak. Greenbrier called it one of the weakest production environments in over a decade and cut FY26 EPS to $3.00-3.15. RSI shows Q2 2026 industry deliveries of 5,527 against 31,205 for all of 2025. Wabtec itself forecast North American railcar builds down ~21% in 2026, so this drag on the Components line sits inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Components weakness was part of the Feb 2025 miss (-9.06%), but in 2026 it has been absorbed by locomotive equipment growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Already in the company's guide (-21% build), so mostly priced. It is filed because Greenbrier's guide cut after Wabtec last spoke confirms the trough has not turned.
findings.independence: Greenbrier commentary: https://www.freightwaves.com/news/greenbrier-racks-up-600-million-in-new-railcar-orders. Wabtec's -21% build forecast: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/wabtec-q2-earnings-call-highlights. Netted against the rest of the company: Freight Equipment grew +35% in Q2 on locomotives and Transit +18.9%, so Components is a minority line.

findings.finding: The buyback is running at about $230M a quarter: $243M in Q1 and $218M in Q2, ~1.8M shares in H1, per the 10-Q. If it continued at that pace, Q3's diluted share count falls by about 1% sequentially, a mechanical support to EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to the buyback line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely in consensus already; it is filed only as part of why the run-rate argument in finding 1 holds.
findings.independence: This is the same 10-Q as finding 1, but a different line.

findings.finding: Insiders sold three times after the Q2 print: $693k (2026-08-06), $286k by an EVP (2026-08-18) and $867k (2026-08-24). No insider buying was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The amounts are routine for a ~$48B company, the sales are public Form 4s, and they likely reflect post-earnings window selling.
findings.independence: The MarketScreener feed lists all three (https://uk.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/WESTINGHOUSE-AIR-BRAKE-TE-14842/news/).

findings.finding: Near-term maturities: a $500M 2025 Term Credit Agreement due 2026-11-27, $750M of 3.45% notes due in 2026, and $638M drawn on the revolver at June 30. Total debt was $6.57B, with $1.66B current. The money funded the Dellner ($1.05B) and Frauscher acquisitions, both of which are growing, and buybacks. The release or call may address refinancing.
findings.why_not_priced: The debt funds acquisitions that are visibly contributing: Digital +88.5% and Transit +18.9% in Q2. Operating cash flow was $441M in Q2, and the company was in covenant compliance. Read through the financing rule, it is a zero; it is filed only for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Union Pacific (Q3 on 2026-10-22, 07:45 ET) and CSX (Q3 on 2026-10-21 after the close) report locomotive and capex commentary after the WAB exit window closes. Greenbrier reports FQ4 on 2026-10-26.
The $500M 2025 Term Credit Agreement matures 2026-11-27, which is after the window.

No cause for the 20-day drift lower was found in the news; the drift is industrials-wide or unexplained, so it is worth 0.

baseline_tension: The mild up lean agrees with the slight upside skew (-2.03 'upside paid'), but that skew rests on 281 contracts and carries little weight. It cuts mildly against the 20-day drift (-3.6%). The drift has no identified cause, so it is not treated as information.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the run-rate beat finding goes from +0.6 to +0.4. The name's beat-and-raise reactions are uneven (+10.0, +1.5, -2.3), and per rule 3 management's own guidance that margin acceleration comes in Q4 sits inside the finding.
Same concern carried into the scaled number: p_up moves from 55 to 54, applied once.

Rule 6 (verify the bar) was checked: two estimate sources agree ($2.72 and $2.73), so no cap was applied. The guidance finding stays at -0.5 because the street's FY number already sits above the guide midpoint.
Rule 4 (financing): the debt maturity finding was already signed 0 after asking what the money bought (acquisitions that are growing). No change.
Rule 5 (proxies): the AAR and railcar-build findings were already small and labelled as proxies. No change.
